question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

It is 2036. Looking back, 5 landmark papers each settled this question in a way that surprised the field, because of how they approached it. For each paper, describe what it measured, analyzed, or did, as a concrete idea a research lab could pursue today. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Time-resolved AP-1 degradation during consolidation (imagined 2036 paper 1)
ideas.description: The paper used auxin-inducible degrons on endogenous c-Fos and JunB to remove AP-1 at defined windows after a learning-like stimulus, then scored later recall. Labs can replicate this with rapid degron tags, asking whether memory needs AP-1 during induction, during a consolidation window, or only at retrieval.

ideas.title: Persistence of AP-1 motif accessibility after stimulus washout (imagined 2036 paper 2)
ideas.description: The study tracked AP-1 motif accessibility and occupancy in single cells with paired ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag over days after stimulus removal, separating chromatin states that persist from transcription that has returned to baseline. A lab could run this in primary neurons or T cells, with the key readout being whether accessibility outlasts AP-1 binding.

ideas.title: Enhancer-level memory tested by re-induction kinetics (imagined 2036 paper 3)
ideas.description: Researchers measured how quickly previously stimulated enhancers respond to a second stimulus, using CRISPRi or dCas9 blocking of AP-1 sites and CUT&RUN for H3K27ac and 3D contacts. The test is whether faster or stronger re-induction depends on enhancer marks that outlast AP-1 occupancy.

ideas.title: Optogenetic reactivation of AP-1-tagged ensembles to test sufficiency (imagined 2036 paper 4)
ideas.description: The team tagged cells that were active during an AP-1 pulse with a light- or drug-inducible label, then reactivated only those cells optogenetically to see whether behavior or a downstream program was restored. A lab could adapt activity-dependent tagging systems to AP-1 target promoters to ask whether reactivating the tagged population is enough to recall the state.

ideas.title: Reconstitution of AP-1 on nucleosomal templates with ligand withdrawal (imagined 2036 paper 5)
ideas.description: The paper reconstituted AP-1 with nucleosome-containing templates in vitro and measured dimer dwell time, nucleosome remodeling, and residual accessibility after the activating signal was removed. A lab could reproduce this with purified Fos/Jun and defined chromatin, using phosphosite or bZIP domain mutants to separate binding-dependent from remodeling-dependent memory.
